environment: 4 CPUs, no GPU, SwiftShader software raster. Absolute numbers are read relative to the P3-0 baseline, taken on the same kind of machine. A slow frame with about 0 ms of main-thread work is a raster wait (environment-scaled). A long animation frame (LoAF) with real script or layout work is an app cost.
scoreNote: A low 3. The default (Lenis) path meets the headless floors at both widths, and 3 of the 4 named sections clear 1.5x. Six things keep it from a 4: the intro regressed on the same machine; CLS is not 0 in any run; the main thread is not quiet after the titles (real script, 83 to 367 ms); idle-time tasks of up to 500 ms land during scroll flings; the act-1 opening card is now the slowest transition on the page (4.8 fps against 26.2 for the old act-1); and three designed effects end in one-frame cuts. The native path, which uses the same scroll driver as the baseline, regressed (15.2 to 10.2 fps; 27 to 42 pops).

findings.finding: The act-1 opening card (iris -> ship -> journal) is the slowest transition on the page: 4.8 fps, p95 733 ms, max 800 ms at 1440, against 26.2 fps for the old act-1. It is also the lowest card at 1024 (11.6 fps). The longest LoAFs are 790 / 717 / 558 ms with 0-6 ms of work, so they are raster-bound, but this is relative to the other cards (act-3 and act-4 run at 20-21 fps on the same machine). On screen at once: 4 masks, 18 promoted layers, 14 infinite animations, and the hero's layers in #top repaint 20x under the card. The worst reader clips are #29 (3.2 fps, 567 ms) and #30 (4.0 fps, 517 ms).

A 500 ms idle-time task (block 456 ms) runs in the middle of a fling. It is the single worst app-caused stall in the round. The same idle task appears at 1024 (248 ms, optuna-screener, skimmer-1024 #31), at act-1 in reader-1440 (288 ms, #27), and as 120-171 ms slices while the director's cut starts (#2-#4). Idle work is not bounded to a short slice and does not wait for scrolling to stop.

The main thread is not quiet after the titles (§12.1). In the 3 s after quiet-end, while the reader begins to scroll, there is real script: an idle callback of 225 ms plus an 83 ms one, an unattributed rAF callback of 128-161 ms, and in the motion intro run a 367 ms idle callback. This is the warm-up ladder firing on the first scroll. It also pulls the intro's 'top' section from 54.5 fps (baseline) to 21.3 fps.
findings.cause: app (the unattributed rAF callback may be the capture tool's)

Card stages and other fixed layers keep repainting outside their own sections. The act-2 stage repaints in journey and trading-algos; act-3 in films (x115) and beyond (x42); act-4 in writing, voices, principles and contact; the journey sticky column in top, about and act-2; the trading-algos window in optuna-screener; the #intro / #intro-stage layer in act-1 through trading-algos in the native, alt and gl runs (x14-46). Finished or not-yet-started layers should cost nothing.

The page should be standing still, but some sections still repaint. Journey runs at 7.3 fps at rest at 1440 (raster 104.6 ms/s, 3.3 paints/s, the sticky column plus a full-bleed overlay) and 52.1 fps at 1024; the baseline was 60 / 0 ms/s. act-4 runs at 41.6 fps at rest (68.2 ms/s, act-card-shape repaints 10.7/s) and act-1 at 30.7 fps. Top reads 0.6 fps at 1440 only (60.3 at 1024), with the hero video repainting: probably environment (software video decode), but re-run it.

In the act-2 seam card, the act title used as a mask ('The Workshop' / 'Work') appears in one frame (17-44 % of the frame changes) and, at 1024, drops away in one frame (28.6 %). It reads as a cut rather than a dissolve.

findings.finding: With native scrolling (the baseline's driver), the page regressed against P3-0: 10.2 against 15.2 fps at 1440, and 42 against 27 pops. The card sections that used to be cheap are now costly (act-1 28.8 -> 4.1, act-4 38 -> 8.1, credits 40 -> 14.9), while the raster diet paid off in work (3.2 -> 8.4), journey (3.5 -> 7.5), kill-list (3.9 -> 7.3) and writing (5.0 -> 9.4). Principles and contact show full-frame jumps without any scroll movement (diff 79-101).
The alt variant blocks the main thread 6.5x as long as the default at 1440 (3,749 against 573 ms) and 3x at 1024 (1,940 against 619 ms), with 21 / 13 pops. Look at it before alt ships.

Counted by duration, the LoAF and INP failures are SwiftShader raster waits: warm-up probe worst work 12 / 14 ms, intro blocking 17 / 30 ms, and INP 688 ms with 0 ms input delay. The games themselves are smooth: the drone flies at about 55-60 fps (119 frames in 2,149 ms), and Dead Eye slows time correctly.

findings.finding: Where two stars run at once, frame rate and stalls get worse: B18+B19 (569 ms overlap) coincides with the 500 ms idle task, and B45-B47 sit in writing/voices. One star at a time is also the cheaper option.

recommendations: 1. Keep the main thread free while people scroll. No idle-time or warm-up task should run longer than about 10-15 ms per slice; the warm-up steps should wait until scrolling has been still for a beat, and never run in the 3 s after the titles. Split the first-scroll visibility pass (now 180-350 ms in one callback) so it measures a few elements per frame or only those near the viewport. The ~100 ms of work when journey is entered and the 60-120 ms animation frames in kill-list and films should be spread across frames or prepared ahead.

2. Make finished and not-yet-started layers free. When a card's stage is not on screen (before its card, or after it ends), take it out of painting entirely, not just to zero opacity. The same applies to the intro layer after the hand-off, the journey sticky column outside journey, the trading-algos window outside its section, and the voices sticky layer in principles. This is what holds principles (4.9 fps) and contact (1.8 fps) down, and it is the cheapest win on the page.

3. Lighten the act-1 opening card: fewer things alive at once (14 infinite animations, 4 masks, 18 promoted layers on screen). Stop the hero's ambient loops once the card covers the hero, and run the iris reveal as a pure move/fade of an already-drawn layer, so it no longer redraws the plate every frame.

4. Bring CLS to 0. Give the scrubbed sentences and the world-face captions line boxes that don't change when the film font arrives (metric-matched fallback, or reserve the final width and height). Make the writing title animate without moving layout. Make the reduced-motion layout final at first paint, removing the 0.06-0.12 about/journey jump. Reserve the play-screen graphic's space.

5. Replace the one-frame cuts with eased exits. The act-2 title mask should dissolve in and out over 200-300 ms or follow the scroll. The act-4 hall flash should decay over at least 300 ms rather than dropping in one frame. At the films hand-off, the next block should be drawn and placed a viewport early and arrive by a fade or move, so it doesn't fill in or jump.

6. Intro: have the name and the hero's controls already drawn under the intro, so they are visible on the 2nd reveal frame, without the all-at-once fill-in during the titles. Prepare the hero layer before the wipe so the hold/reveal does not stall (0.34-0.59 s here), and keep the 3 s after the titles free of script (see 1).

7. Stop idle repaints. At rest, nothing in journey or the act-4 card should redraw (journey 7.3 fps and act-4 41.6 fps at rest at 1440). Any ambient motion there should be a move or fade of a drawn layer, or stop when the page stops.

8. Native (no Lenis) path, lower priority: in principles and contact, scrubbed and time-driven effects should step smoothly between wheel notches rather than jump (full-frame diffs of 79-101 with no scroll movement). Recheck pops against the baseline's driver, not only under Lenis.

9. Measurement: re-run the 1440 idle probe on the hero (0.6 fps, which looks environmental), and do the §12.1 real-laptop pass (p95 <= 20 ms; no frame > 50 ms in the cards, the intro and the cut) before calling the motion done. Most of the raster-wait jank should shrink on a GPU; recommendations 1, 2, 4 and 5 will not shrink on their own.
